chunks: Have you not seen how your Lord lengthens out the shadow? He could have kept it motionless if He liked. Yet We make the sun its pilot to show the way.
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the shadow's movement mentioned in Surah Al-Furqan?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited as a rational proof (dalil) for the unity and omnipotence of God, illustrating how natural phenomena like the shifting shadow serve as subtle signs of divine will. The phrase 'if He willed, He would make it stationary' emphasizes God's absolute power over creation, while the sun acts as the visible mechanism (dala'il) that governs this movement, reinforcing the concept of tawhid through observable cosmic order.
